claims.text: Vault is not open source; it uses the Business Source License model.
Pulumi ESC is fully open source and Apache 2.0 licensed.
Vault stores secrets only, whereas Pulumi ESC stores environments, secrets, and configurations.
Pulumi ESC environments can be composed from multiple other environments, so shared configuration is inherited rather than duplicated.
Pulumi ESC environments can reference secrets stored in Vault, and those secrets can be organized as collections that are versioned, branched, and composed inside other collections.
Pulumi ESC can store non-secret configuration alongside secrets kept in Vault.
Vault is licensed under Business Source License 1.1.
Vault offers a hosted cloud service and self-hosting, and self-hosting requires significant management overhead.
Vault's editor offers a key/value form editor with a JSON toggle.
The vault CLI reads and writes secrets but does not inject them as environment variables.
Vault Agent's process supervisor mode can inject secrets as environment variables.
Vault has no equivalent concept to composable environments; secrets are organized by path convention and structure is maintained by hand.
Vault has no first-class environment to reference, so secrets are read by path; no secret-referencing equivalent.
Pulumi ESC supports built-in functions such as toJSON, fromJSON, fromBase64, and toString.
Vault provides templating and transformation functions, such as username templating and the Transform secrets engine, but not functions for composing configuration values.
Vault cloud secrets engines generate short-lived credentials for AWS, Azure, and Google Cloud.
Each Vault cloud secrets engine is configured with a static credential that Vault uses to mint short-lived credentials.
